public.prompt: A reusable author badge needs spacing after its avatar in the direction text flows. It must work in left-to-right, right-to-left, and vertical writing modes without locale-specific selectors. Which declaration expresses that intent?

options.label: Set `margin-inline-end` on the avatar so the mapped physical side follows writing mode and direction.
Set `margin-right` on the avatar and swap it to `margin-left` only when the document direction is RTL.
Set `margin-block-end` on the avatar so the spacing follows the edge where inline text finishes.

answerProof.summary: `margin-inline-end` represents the end edge of the inline text-flow axis. Its physical mapping follows both direction and writing mode, avoiding separate horizontal locale rules and covering vertical flow.
decisiveConstraints: Spacing belongs after the avatar along the inline axis.
The inline axis may run horizontally or vertically.
The component cannot depend on locale-specific selector overrides.

claims.statement: `margin-inline-end` maps to a physical margin according to writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

optionRationales.explanation: The logical property follows the inline end in all declared writing directions without physical-side branching.
Left and right overrides cover horizontal directions but do not map the spacing onto a vertical inline axis.
optionRationales.plausibility: Direction selectors are a familiar way to mirror horizontal layouts between LTR and RTL.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The same rule must adapt when inline content flows vertically.

optionRationales.explanation: `margin-block-end` follows the block-stacking axis rather than the edge after inline content.
optionRationales.plausibility: The word end matches the desired trailing edge and block margins often separate component content.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The spacing must follow the inline axis, not the axis along which blocks stack.
